title: PropX rooftop attributes
description: Output contract for outputs/roof_attributes.json (design section 8). The schema is a policy document as much as a validator: it forbids publishing a CV polygon as the primary outline, forbids an attribute without provenance, forbids a confidence without a method, a rationale or the not-calibrated note, and closes every object it safely can so a typo fails the run instead of shipping.

availability.description: Provenance vocabulary from design section 5. Closed: an unrecognised word here is a bug, not a new category.

confidence.description: A documented heuristic reliability indicator. score is null when no value was produced. factors carries every multiplicative penalty by name, so the score can be recomputed by hand.

factors.description: At most three penalties, each in [0.5, 1.0] (design section 6). Enforced here as well as in code, so a hand-edited document cannot smuggle in a fourth.

note.description: Emitted by types.Confidence.as_dict. const, so no document can be published without it.
note.const: Documented heuristic reliability indicator, not a calibrated probability.

conflict.description: Authoritative value versus image evidence (design section 5.1). Records the disagreement; never a correction.

image_evidence.description: An independent image observation, reported alongside an authoritative value rather than replacing it.

attribute.description: One published attribute. value may be any JSON type including null, but the pairing is constrained (RTI-014): a determined availability (authoritative/derived/observed/inferred) requires a non-null value AND a numeric confidence score, and an absent availability (unavailable/not_in_source) requires a null value AND a null score — so a hand-edited document cannot ship a value with no availability to back it, or an abstention wearing a score. requires_review/review_reasons are machine-readable per-attribute review routing (RTI-004): present only together, and only when the published value's own evidence is marginal. A review flag is an invitation to look, never an edit.

measure.description: e.g. "planimetric" — stated in-record so an area is never read as a roof-surface area.

source_detail.description: Layer, field and raw source value. Left open: source field names are preserved verbatim and vary by layer.

requires_review.description: Emitted only when true: the value is published unchanged but its own evidence is marginal and a human should look.

position.description: One coordinate pair, lon/lat order. Exactly two numbers: every geometry in this contract is 2D, so a third element would be data the pipeline never produced.

linear_ring.description: A closed ring needs at least 4 positions (triangle + closing repeat). An emptier ring is not a degenerate geometry, it is a bug.

polygon_rings.description: Exterior ring first, then interior rings. minItems 1: a Polygon with no rings — coordinates [] — is invalid (RTI-014).

polygon.description: GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon with the nesting depth pinned per type (RTI-014), so a MultiPolygon's coordinates pasted into a Polygon — or an empty coordinates array — fails validation instead of shipping. crs is required wherever a geometry appears: coordinates without a stated frame are numbers, not a location.

authoritative_polygon.description: The primary outline. polygon_source is required because a reader must be able to tell the 2025 roof record from the FMZK fallback dissolve (design section 3.2).

agreement.description: Agreement between two related estimates, not segmentation accuracy: the CV polygon is seeded from the authoritative outline (design section 4.1).

exterior_iou.description: IoU after removing interior rings from BOTH geometries. The figure boundary_alignment_warning is measured against, because it cannot be moved by a hole-count mismatch.

hausdorff_m.description: Symmetric Hausdorff distance between the EXTERIOR rings only. Redefined in Phase 4A: a polygon's .boundary includes interior rings, so the previous all-rings figure conflated edge disagreement with hole-count mismatch. The all-rings value is retained as hausdorff_full_boundary_m.

hausdorff_full_boundary_m.description: The previous all-rings symmetric Hausdorff distance, retained so nothing is lost. Sensitive to interior-ring topology and therefore NOT used by boundary_alignment_warning.

delineation.description: Who delineated what. primary_polygon is a const, so the schema itself forbids publishing a CV polygon as the primary outline (design section 4).

status.description: Present only when flag is true. Same requires_visual_review marker used by an attribute conflict, so both routes to human inspection read alike. When this fires, the record's top-level review_flags array also carries a boundary_alignment_warning entry, so review_flags is the single complete answer to 'what needs a human?'.

topology_mismatch.description: DIAGNOSTIC, not a review trigger. Reports differing interior-ring counts between the authoritative outline and the CV candidate. The candidate segmenter discards holes below its configured minimum area, so a mismatch is expected behaviour rather than a finding about the roof, and it deliberately carries no requires_visual_review status.

failure_reason.description: Segmentation not converging is a reportable outcome, not an error.

fmzk_crosscheck.description: Cross-check only (design section 1.4). matched_by is a const: boundary identity was tested on real geometry and rejected, so best geometric overlap is the only join rule the output can express.

cardinality.description: Read in the direction given by cardinality_basis: BW_GEB_ID building unit -> authoritative roof records. 1:1 = one unit, one roof record. 1:n = one unit carrying several roof records (the documented Seestadt cases 5729190 -> 4 and 5576077 -> 2); every competing record id is listed in competing_roof_record_ids and none is averaged or chosen. unmatched = no unit overlapped the roof record. 'n:1' is intentionally not a permitted value, because reversing the orientation silently inverts the meaning of the join.

cardinality_basis.description: Fixed orientation for every cardinality value in this document, published so the notation cannot be misread.

aggregation.description: applied stays false unless an explicit, reasoned aggregation was configured; 1:n joins are never silently averaged (design section 1.4 rule 5).

trigger.description: Closed: a trigger nobody documented is a bug, not a new category. low_judgeability / weak_cv_agreement / withheld_attributes are evidence-driven triggers fed by measured per-building quantities (RTI-004); visual_audit_questionable routes the transcribed model-assisted visual audit of an earlier baseline into the same review stream — a report, never an edit.

attributes.description: Closed vocabulary from the design section 5 table. A misspelled attribute name fails the run rather than appearing as a new field nobody documented. roof_area_m2, roof_type and mean_slope_deg are always emitted — absent source data becomes availability not_in_source, never a missing key.

visual_surface_appearance.description: Renamed from roof_surface_class (RTI-017): the value is a visible surface APPEARANCE, never a material or construction class. null is an abstention - too little of the roof judgeable, or a dominance margin weaker than the classifier resolves.

solar_panels.description: WITHHELD AFTER A FAILED EVALUATION. The RGB detector produced 1 false positive on 35 held-out reference-negative roofs and failed the pre-registered bar of zero. The reference was made by reading the same imagery rather than independent ground truth and contains only two positives in total, so it supports neither recall nor a general accuracy claim. No Boolean is published: value is always null, availability is 'unavailable' and confidence.score is always null. Raw candidate diagnostics remain under image_evidence.quality for a future independent validation.

green_roof.description: Three-state value domain (RTI-009): detected / not_detected / null. not_detected is a statement about this imagery over a sufficiently judgeable roof; null is an abstention and never a negative. Booleans are forbidden so absence of evidence cannot be published as evidence of absence.

cv_candidate_polygon.description: null on segmentation failure, which is a reportable outcome and not an error.

audit_basis.description: Which artifact the visual audit actually examined. audited_document_sha256 + baseline_commit identify the EARLIER baseline the reviewers saw; reaudit_of_artifact_sha256 stays null until a human review of a final artifact records that artifact's sha256 here (propx-roofs record-review), together with reaudit_overlays (per-overlay sha256s of the reviewed files), reaudit_reviewer and reaudit_date. Consumers must treat any document whose own sha256 differs from both as carrying baseline-only audit evidence; the strict release gate additionally requires the reaudit_* fields to match the current artifacts byte for byte.

reaudit_overlays.description: Overlay path -> sha256 of the file the human review examined; written by record-review, present only once a review of a final artifact is recorded.

building_manual_review.description: Per-building report block attaching the transcribed MODEL-ASSISTED visual audit (validation/audit_annotations.json). QA report only, of an earlier baseline identified in audit_basis: it is not human ground truth, it asserts nothing about this document's values, and no value, geometry or confidence can be derived from it — the pipeline has no code path from this block to published content (design section 7). Embedded annotations are the slim form (aspect/status/code/summary); the verbatim note stays in the annotations file that detail_ref points at, so the artifact does not duplicate the full audit paragraphs per building.

status.description: Closed audit vocabulary. questionable/conflicts additionally produce a visual_audit_questionable review flag; the published value stands unchanged in every case.

code.description: Stable machine key, always exactly aspect.status.

summary.description: Concise faithful distillation of the audit's verbatim note, which remains in validation/audit_annotations.json under this building's id (see detail_ref). Never an upgraded or softened assessment.

detail_ref.description: Pointer to this building's full annotation entries, verbatim notes included.

licence.description: Per-source licence, read from the source's own entry in configs/study_area.yaml (RTI-019). Every current source is 'CC BY 4.0' (Stadt Wien) and that stays the recorded value, but the schema requires a non-empty string rather than that constant so a future differently-licensed source is a config edit, not a contract change.

attribution.description: Per-source attribution string, read from the source's own config entry; non-empty because unattributed data cannot be published under an attribution licence.

schema_version.description: Version of this output contract. The const below is the single source of truth: propx_roofs.provenance.schema_version() reads it from the packaged schema, so a document stamped with any other value is invalid by construction. Bump it here when the contract changes shape. 1.1.0: run provenance members (git/runtime/dependencies/cache), tri-state green_roof, visual_surface_appearance rename, evidence-driven review triggers, per-attribute requires_review routing, manual_review audit blocks, and the RTI-014 validity constraints. 1.2.0: slim embedded audit annotations (aspect/status/code/summary + detail_ref instead of duplicated verbatim notes) and the optional reaudit_* human-review record in audit_basis.

algorithm_parameters_hash.description: Fingerprint of the in-code algorithm parameter VALUES in propx_roofs.segment.SEGMENT_PARAMS and propx_roofs.attributes.ATTRIBUTE_PARAMS, which config_hash does not cover: sha256 of a canonical JSON payload, truncated to 16 hex characters. It is NOT a source-code hash and NOT a hash of the whole algorithm - a code change that leaves every parameter value equal leaves this field unchanged, so two runs agreeing here can still differ in output. Where configs/pipeline.yaml overrides a default, the override is covered by config_hash and this field still reports the in-code default; only the two hashes together determine the effective parameters.

git.description: The commit the pipeline code ran as, captured via git at run time. commit/dirty are null - with a note saying why - when git or a checkout is unavailable (e.g. an installed wheel); a null is honest, a fabricated SHA is not. dirty=true means the working tree had uncommitted changes, so the commit alone does not identify the code.

runtime.description: Interpreter and platform of the run. Byte-identical reproduction is only claimed for the pinned runtime recorded here; other runtimes are expected to reproduce semantically, not byte-for-byte.

dependencies.description: Installed versions (importlib.metadata) of the dependencies that decide numeric output. null when a distribution cannot be resolved in the running environment - recorded, never guessed.

cache.description: The input cache this run read (RTI-011). manifest_sha256 is the sha256 of data/cache/<area>/manifest.json, which itself hashes every raw input file, so this one value pins the run's entire input state. verified reports the outcome of actually running the cache verifier against that cache - a measurement, not an assertion. A missing manifest is an honest null with a note.

crs_metric.description: Every published metric value comes from this projected CRS (Amendment B3). Web Mercator area error at Vienna's latitude is ~2.2x, so EPSG:3857 is not permitted here.

confidence_note.const: Heuristic reliability indicators, not calibrated probabilities. Not validated against labelled ground truth.

sample_note.const: The 8–10 buildings form a purposive sample selected for attribute diversity, source availability, and visual interpretability. They are not statistically representative of Vienna's building stock.

manual_review.description: QA only. Review cannot mutate, promote or override any pipeline output (design section 7); this block reports whether anyone has looked. visual_qa_of_baseline_attached means the transcribed MODEL-ASSISTED visual audit of the EARLIER baseline named in audit_basis travels with this document as per-building report blocks — deliberately not 'reviewed', because that word would claim a human sign-off of these bytes that never happened.
